widgets_values:
Exercise: reading the time from an analog clock (skeleton + k-means, fully composable)

The 'Clock Dial' subgraph finds the dial: Canny edges -> longest contour -> 'CV Enclosing Circle' (center + radius). The 'Clock Hands (skeleton + k-means)' subgraph is built entirely from generic point/shape utilities: an Otsu inverse threshold turns everything dark into a mask; 'CV Select Component At Point' keeps only the blob connected to the dial center (numerals, ticks and the rim are separate components and vanish); 'CV Skeletonize' thins the blob to 1-px centerlines, so each hand contributes pixels in proportion to its LENGTH - a numeral that touches a hand collapses to a short compact stroke instead of a cloud of corners and can no longer outvote the hand; cv2.findNonZero turns the skeleton into a point set; 'CV Filter Points By Distance' keeps the outer ones (0.25r-1.05r); 'CV Points To Polar' turns them into unit direction vectors, which the 'CV K-Means Points' subgraph clusters for k=2 AND k=3 - if the k=2 clustering is loose (mean_sq_distance > 0.05, checked with 'GreaterThan'), the clock has 3 hands and if/else picks the k=3 labels. 'CV Reduce Values By Label' (mode = densest value, circular period 360) finds each cluster's hand angle as the SPIKE of its angle distribution: the hand's collinear pixels all share one bearing while a fused numeral smears over 10-25 degrees, so it shifts the cluster mean and even the median but never the mode. 'CV Reduce Points By Label' (farthest from origin) gives each cluster's tip + hand length; 'CV Pick Value' selects the shortest hand's angle (hour) and the longest / 2nd-longest one's (minute; with 3 hands the longest is the second hand). The 'Clock Angles to Time' subgraph converts angles with MathExpression: minute = round(a / 6) % 60, hour = ((round((a - b * 0.5) / 30) - 1) % 12) + 1.

Inspect the detection visually on TWO previews. The evidence preview ('CV Draw Points') marks the skeleton points colored by cluster with the per-cluster tip points as big white dots - raw evidence, so the tip dot may sit on a fused numeral. The FINAL-reading preview shows the actual decision: 'CV Polar To Points' turns each cluster's mode angle + reach back into image coordinates, 'CV Draw Rays' draws the detected hands from the dial center, and 'CV Draw Text' prints the time (composed with Basic data handling's to-STRING / zfill / concat) - what you see there is exactly what the workflow decided. The tips array, n_hands and the found flag are also inspectable. Failure tolerance: every point node treats empty/None as a valid result, so an image without a clock yields found=false and both previews show the unmodified photo.

Tips: works on frontal photos with hands darker than the dial; for light hands on a dark dial switch the threshold to THRESH_BINARY | THRESH_OTSU. A second hand is assumed to be the longest - on clocks where it is not, swap the Pick Value ranks.

widgets_values:
CV K-Means Points

Clusters a point set into k groups (cv2.kmeans), the point-array sibling of the 'CV K-Means Colors' and 'CV K-Means Mask Clusters' blueprints.

k is clamped to the number of points. 'mean_sq_distance' (the average squared distance of the points to their cluster center) measures how well k fits: run this twice with different k and compare, e.g. with 'Basic data handling: GreaterThan' + if/else, to choose the cluster count - that is how the clock exercise decides between two and three hands.

Zero points are valid: 'success' is false, 'labels' and 'centers' come back empty and nothing raises. cv2.kmeans itself asserts on an empty sample set, so the data path swaps in a one-point dummy and the result path throws it away.
